# Codex Cryptica

> A private, local-first campaign manager for lore keepers who value privacy, speed, visual organisation, and AI-assisted worldbuilding.

## Core Product

- [Codex Cryptica](https://codexcryptica.com/): The primary entry point. A free, local-first RPG campaign manager and worldbuilding tool.
- [Full User Guide & Features](https://codexcryptica.com/llms-full.txt): Complete AI-readable feature and help documentation.

## Key Features

- Knowledge Graph: Visualise entities and relationships as an interactive node-link diagram.
- AI Oracle: Context-aware lore assistant powered by Google Gemini — optional, vault-aware.
- Local-First Storage: Vault data is stored in the browser using OPFS. No cloud account required.
- Map & VTT Mode: Use maps, pins, fog of war, tokens, initiative, and tactical play.
- Spatial Canvas: Build conspiracy boards, quest flows, faction webs, and relationship maps.
- Markdown Ownership: All vault files are plain Markdown with YAML frontmatter — no lock-in.
- Offline Support: The wiki, graph, timeline, and canvas work fully without internet access.

## Privacy & AI Policy

Codex Cryptica is local-first: vault data is stored locally by default and does not require a cloud account. AI features are optional. When AI features are used, only the selected or retrieved context needed for that request is sent to the configured AI provider. Read the full responsible AI principles at https://codexcryptica.com/responsible-ai-worldbuilding.

## Live In-Browser Generators

The pages above are informational landing pages; these are the canonical, no-login-required tools that actually generate and let you save a draft into a vault. The `/tools/*` pages above link into these for the interactive experience.

- [Generators Hub](https://codexcryptica.com/generators): Directory of every live in-browser RPG generator, grouped by genre.
<!-- LLMS-GENERATORS:START -->
- [Random RPG Idea Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/random): Draws from every generator at once, for a reader who wants a prompt rather than a specific artefact.
- [RPG NPC Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/npc): Create NPCs across any genre with secrets, faction ties, and table-ready hooks. Works without login, then imports into your local Codex vault.
- [D&D NPC Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/dnd-npc): Create a fantasy NPC with ancestry, role, personality traits, a hidden secret, and a table-ready GM hook. Works without login, then imports into your local vault.
- [Personality Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/personality): Create a personality you can actually portray at the table: what they want, how they act under pressure, how they speak, and the one contradiction that makes them feel human. Works without login, then imports into your local vault.
- [Settlement Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/settlement): Generate an inhabited place that answers three questions: why does it exist, who really controls it, and what is about to go wrong. Works for any genre — fantasy, cyberpunk, sci-fi, horror, post-apocalyptic, and more.
- [Tavern Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/tavern): Create a campaign-ready tavern with atmosphere, owner, notable patrons, rumours, and a hidden problem. Works without login, then imports into your local vault.
- [Social Hub Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/social-hub): Create a campaign-ready social venue for any genre. Pick your setting, venue type, and atmosphere — get a named location with regulars, rumours, and a hidden problem.
- [Kingdom Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/kingdom): Create a campaign-ready fantasy realm with a ruler, major factions, internal tensions, and adventure hooks. Works without login, then imports into your local vault.
- [Nation Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/nation): Create a campaign-ready political entity for any genre. Pick your setting and polity type — get a named state with power blocs, internal tensions, and adventure hooks.
- [RPG Faction Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/faction): Forge campaign-ready organizations across any genre. Use it as a fantasy guild generator, cyberpunk megacorp creator, sci-fi empire builder, or gothic vampire clan generator with distinct agendas, conflicts, and NPCs.
- [Faction Roster Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/faction-roster): Turn a faction from an organization on paper into the people the party can actually meet, recruit, threaten, or betray — each with a personal motive, a stance toward the faction, and a connection to another member on the roster.
- [Secret Society Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/secret-society): Build a reusable society with a belief, ritual, public cover, secret truth, and immediate hooks for your campaign.
- [Council Vote Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/council-vote): Create a campaign-ready political vote — a council of named voters with different motives, alliances, secrets, and demands, plus a deadline and a voting threshold. Works without login, then imports into your local vault.
- [Heist Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/heist): Build a playable heist instead of a planning session. You get a concrete objective, a prize that is awkward to move, three layered security rings that each allow more than one approach, a five-state alarm track, and a getaway whose original route has already failed. Works without login, then imports into your local vault.
- [Holiday & Festival Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/holiday): Create observances that feel like they grew from a society's history, climate, beliefs, and conflicts. Generate one memorable day or a coherent calendar, from celebratory festivals to contested memorials, without needing an account.
- [BBEG / Campaign Villain Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/bbeg-generator): Create a campaign antagonist who functions as a campaign engine: a goal, motivation, methods, lieutenants, an escalating plan the party can discover and disrupt, and consequences whether they act or not. Works without login, then imports into your local vault.
- [Comic Book Event Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/comic-book-event-generator): Create a large, crossover-tier superhero crisis a campaign can build an arc around: a premise, a staged escalation the party can witness and intervene in, and concrete, campaign-persistent consequences — a location changed, an institution's trust broken, a hero unmasked — not just a premise that resets to normal. Works without login, then imports into your local vault.
- [Superhero Origin Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/origin-generator): Build a superhero origin that is more than a backstory paragraph: a concrete origin event, at least one campaign hook a GM can use tonight, and an ongoing consequence that stays unresolved. Works without login, then imports into your local vault.
- [Superhero Villain Scheme Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/villain-scheme-generator): Create an ongoing villain plot for a Superhero / Comic Book campaign: an objective, why they want it, what they're doing right now, resources and minions, escalating scheme stages the heroes can discover and disrupt, complications, and consequences if nobody intervenes. Any villain -- existing or freshly imagined -- can be running it. Works without login, then imports into your local vault.
- [Creature Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/creature): Create table-ready monsters, beasts, alien fauna, undead, constructs, and mounts across any genre. Generates distinctive appearance, sensory signs, ecological roles, tactical combat behaviour, harvestable remains, and adventure hooks beyond just fighting them.
- [Alien Race Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/alien-race): Build an alien species that is genuinely non-human. Every biological and environmental trait changes something else — six limbs reach their tools and architecture, chemical speech changes what privacy means, a long life reshapes their politics.
- [RPG Encounter Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/encounter): Create playable encounters your players can actually interact with, not just a monster list. Set the encounter type, environment, and threat, then import into your local vault.
- [RPG Quest Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/quest): Create campaign-ready adventure seeds and quest hooks. Set the genre, tone, threat, and twist, then import into your local vault.
- [RPG Rumour Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/rumour): Create a d6 table of six local rumours the party can overhear and choose to chase. Four are essentially true, one is exaggerated, and one is a dangerous misconception. Every rumour names a real lead; the truth stays hidden in GM notes until someone investigates.
- [RPG Puzzle Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/puzzle): Build thematic encounter puzzles that give every player a way to contribute. Get layered clues, alternate solutions, and consequences that keep your adventure moving.
- [Dungeon / Delve Idea Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/dungeon-generator): Create rich, multi-layered dungeons, ancient ruins, abandoned facilities, or subterranean vaults for any RPG genre or world theme. Generates evocative premises, original histories, current operational states, signature landmarks, active conflicts, sectors, factions, hazards, secrets, treasures, and adventure hooks. Every generated delve can also become a fully explorable, room-by-room map — the interactive Dungeon Canvas is exclusive to Codex Cryptica, free to open once you're in the app.
- [Adventure Idea Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/adventure-generator): Create rich, multi-layered adventure scenarios across any RPG genre or world theme. Generates initial situations, primary pressures, key locations, key actors, threats, discoveries, complications, stakes, and non-linear possible outcomes — a situation, not a plot.
- [Adventure Idea Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/adventure-idea-generator): Create rich, multi-layered adventure scenarios across any RPG genre or world theme. Generates initial situations, primary pressures, key locations, key actors, threats, discoveries, complications, stakes, and non-linear possible outcomes — a situation, not a plot.
- [Plot Twist & Complication Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/plot-twist-generator): Turn an established situation into a fair, playable reversal or complication. Keep the facts that matter, overturn an assumption, and give the players new choices.
- [Magic Item Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/magic-item): Create a campaign-ready magic item with lore, abilities, and quirks. Works without login.
- [Minor Magic Item & Trinket Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/minor-magic-item): Generate small-scale, consumable, and limited-use magic items, charms, alchemical draughts, and curiosities designed for creative problem-solving rather than numerical stat bloat. Works without login.
- [RPG Artifact & Relic Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/artifact-generator): Create legendary artifacts and ancient relics with deep lore, multi-tier powers (dormant, awakened, ascendant), consequential costs, pursuing factions, and adventure hooks. Works without login.
- [RPG Item Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/item): Design magic items, weaponry, or rare relics with customizable properties and history. Works without login.
- [RPG Ship Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/ship-generator): Create a campaign-ready vessel for any RPG genre. Sci-fi starships, fantasy galleons, pirate sloops, steampunk airships — pick the role, scale, and condition and get a ship with a crew, a mission, a problem, and a secret.
- [RPG Pantheon Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/pantheon-generator): Create a campaign-ready pantheon with alliances, cosmic conflicts, and detailed member deities. Works without login, then imports into your local vault.
- [RPG God & Deity Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/god-generator): Design detailed single deities, ancestors, or abstract forces with portfolio, rituals, and myths. Works without login, then imports into your local vault.
- [RPG Name Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/names): Generate names for characters, places, factions, and items in any genre. Pick a vibe and culture, steer with optional context, and copy your favourites.
- [Fantasy Name Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/fantasy-names): Generate fantasy names for characters, places, factions, and items across ten cultural styles. Works without login — copy your favourites for your campaign.
- [RPG Fictional Language Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/language-generator): Create a campaign-ready language profile for your world, culture, or species. Choose fantasy, cyberpunk, gothic noir, space opera, modern conspiracy, post-apocalyptic, or pirate foundations, then customize the result.
- [Sci-Fi World Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/world): Create a detailed sci-fi world for your campaign. Choose its environment, habitability, civilisation, and defining feature, then generate a place with conflicts, locations, and playable hooks.
- [Star System Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/star-system): Create a coherent sci-fi star system for your campaign — not just an astronomical inventory. Choose its system type, genre, civilisation level, character, and scientific realism, then generate a star (or stars), major bodies, factions, resources, hazards, and a system-wide conflict or mystery worth building a campaign around.
- [Constellation Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/constellation): Create a night-sky constellation with a story behind it, not just a random name. Choose its genre, visual impression, practical use, and cultural meaning, then generate a star pattern, the culture that reads meaning into it, an origin myth, when it's visible, what it's used for, and one adventure hook.
- [News Sheet Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/news-sheet-generator): Create an in-world news sheet as a printable player handout — a lead headline, short articles, street rumours, classifieds, and propaganda, shaped by who owns the press. Cyberpunk players know it as a screamsheet; it works just as well as a fantasy broadsheet or a station newsfeed. The GM version holds the truth behind the stories and the adventure hooks.
- [Vampire Clan Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/vampire-clan): Create undead factions with bloodlines, feeding habits, dark agendas, and table-ready hooks. Works without login, then imports into your local Codex vault.
- [Cyberpunk Nomad Clan Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/nomad-clan): Create road-hardened nomad clans with convoy culture, territory routes, internal tensions, and campaign-ready hooks. Works without login, then imports into your local Codex vault.
- [Dark Fantasy Faction Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/dark-fantasy-faction): Create fallen orders, cursed noble houses, plague cults, witch-hunters, corpse guilds, and desperate powers with agendas, secrets, NPCs, and table-ready hooks. Works without login, then imports into your local Codex vault.

## Answer Pages

Concise, self-contained reference answers to real RPG and worldbuilding questions. Each page answers the question directly before any product material.

- [Answers Hub](https://codexcryptica.com/answers): Index of every published answer page.
- [What is a point crawl?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/what-is-a-point-crawl): Mapping an adventure as named locations joined by explicit routes, rather than a hex grid.
- [How do you organise RPG campaign notes?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-organise-rpg-campaign-notes): Durable entity pages, dated session logs, and disposable prep — plus the post-session pass that keeps them true.
- [How do you create a fantasy faction?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-create-a-fantasy-faction): Six questions — goal, obstacle, recruits, limits, assets, next move — that make a faction act on its own.
- [How do you organise NPC relationships?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-organise-npc-relationships): Store relationships as directed, named links with a reason and a visibility, not as ally lists.
- [What makes a good random encounter?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/what-makes-a-good-random-encounter): A situation already in progress, with a reason to be there and an option that is not combat.
- [How do you create a pantheon?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-create-a-pantheon): Build entanglements between gods before assigning domains; five structural moves that generate play.
- [How do you design RPG puzzles that do not stall the game?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-design-rpg-puzzles-that-do-not-stall-the-game): More than one way through, and failure that costs something other than time.
- [What should an RPG settlement contain?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/what-should-an-rpg-settlement-contain): A reason to exist, three or four enterable places, three people who want things, and one unsolved problem.
- [How do you create a believable fictional religion?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-create-a-believable-fictional-religion): Write the practice before the doctrine: one rite, one prohibition, who funds it, and what adherents dispute.
- [How do you generate useful RPG rumours?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-generate-useful-rpg-rumours): Build a six-entry table with four reliable leads, one exaggeration, one dangerous misconception, and named sources and destinations.
- [How do you run a conspiracy campaign?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-run-a-conspiracy-campaign): Decide the truth in full before session one, then design how it leaks; every conclusion needs three routes.

## Curated Generator Examples

Curated raw or lightly edited generator output, with provenance, the settings that produced it, and a short editorial note on what makes it usable.

- [Examples Hub](https://codexcryptica.com/examples): Every published example.
- [Fantasy settlement example: Gull's Roost](https://codexcryptica.com/examples/gulls-roost-coastal-smuggling-town): A coastal smuggling town with a working economy, five points of interest and live adventure hooks.
- [RPG faction example: The Low-Tide Rust](https://codexcryptica.com/examples/the-low-tide-rust-dock-syndicate): A dock syndicate rolled inside the Gull's Roost session, reusing that town's places and people.
- [Cyberpunk district example: Arc Hub](https://codexcryptica.com/examples/arc-hub-augmentation-slum): A vertical augmentation slum governed by a malfunctioning municipal AI.
- [Sci-fi encounter example: The Venting Helix](https://codexcryptica.com/examples/the-venting-helix-derelict-hazard): A derelict-ship hazard with four viable solutions and fail-forward escalation.
- [RPG rumour table example: Six Words from Lowmere](https://codexcryptica.com/examples/lowmere-six-words-rumour-table): Lightly edited six-entry rumour table with player-facing gossip, GM truth notes, named sources, and connected consequences.
